core1a.scientific_construction: For the same ideal gas composition and suitable fixed conditions, sound speed v=k√T, so v²/T is constant for absolute T. It is not proportional to the square root of a Celsius reading. A time measurement can include a fixed offset τ: t_obs=τ+L/v. At a matched thermal state, two different known path lengths give v from their time difference and τ by substitution. Repeating this at another temperature tests whether the inferred speed changes as predicted or whether an apparent change comes from detector timing. The same-gas model does not establish actual humidity, composition or flow. A dropped source question is useful as a warning about measurement/model assumptions, not as scored exam evidence.

worked_anchor.task: At 300 K a gas speed is 300 m/s. At 363 K predict speed under the stipulated model.
worked_anchor.reasoning: 330 m/s, since 363/300=1.21. If a thermometer reports 90 °C rather than 363 K, use absolute temperature.

core1a.model_limits: Only specified ideal/matched conditions; extension relations are supplied, not independently warranted compulsory syllabus scope.

core1b.task: A uniform gas is held at 256 K and then 324 K. At 256 K, paths 2.4 and4.8 m have observed times 12 and22 ms. At 324 K, paths 2.7 and5.4 m have observed times 13 and23 ms. Model X: speed follows k√T, detector delay unchanged. Model Y: speed is constant, delay may change. Test both, identify any alternative supported by the measurements, and predict the time for a 8.1 m path at 324 K under that alternative.
